subject: Capacity prioritization request — StrataGrid SG-4723 (potential conflict with HelioWorks)
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@stratagrid.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity request and conflict notice (SG-4723)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — StrataGrid is excited about moving forward. We have an upcoming feature launch in mid-June that will require sustained low-latency inference. Based on our projections and the test runs, we expect peak sustained throughput equivalent to ~32 A100-class GPUs over a rolling 2-hour window, with short spikes up to ~48 for <30 minutes.

Procurement asked me to share the attached capacity_request_form and our latest term sheet (SG-4723_term_sheet.pdf). We'd like to reserve Dedicated capacity to guarantee latency for our customers. We understand Redwood has other big commitments (you mentioned HelioWorks previously) — please let us know if this request bumps into any allocation constraints or scheduled commitments.

Key ask: can Redwood commit a reserved tranche (32 units baseline, 48 burst) for the June 12–June 30 launch window? If not, what mitigations or alternative timelines do you recommend?

Attachments: capacity_request_form.pdf, SG-4723_term_sheet.pdf

Regards,
Elena Park
Head of Platform Ops, StrataGrid
elena@stratagrid.com
+1 415-555-0190

--
Procurement: procurement@stratagrid.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@stratagrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request and conflict notice (SG-4723)

Elena — thanks for the detail and for sending the forms. I pulled the team in to review. Short answer: we can get you baseline capacity, but we have a timing conflict with an existing committed Reserved customer (HelioWorks, deal HW-9091) during the exact June window you requested. We need to scope a safe plan that preserves your SLA while minimizing impact to both customers.

Next steps I propose now:
- Internal prioritization discussion (cc'd Karthik, Ben, Lauren) to map options.
- We’ll run the attached gpu_sizing_model.xlsx against your workload traces and our fleet calendar to produce a concrete tranche proposal.
- If required, we can offer a hybrid plan: guaranteed baseline (24 units) + burst lane to 48 with preemption policy and traffic shaping for the first two weeks.

I’ve flagged this as an escalation because it affects committed capacity for another enterprise. Karthik/Ben — can you review the attached forms and the HelioWorks calendar and propose a short list of options (A/B/C) by EOD tomorrow? Lauren — please prepare a draft customer note outlining potential mitigations and trade-offs for StrataGrid (including possible credit if we shift their launch).

Elena — appreciate the heads up. We will follow up with a firm plan and timing.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0123
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request and conflict notice (SG-4723)

Team — I ran a quick slice against the fleet schedule and HelioWorks' committed tranche (HW-9091 is 40 reserved units June 1–30). Notes and options below:

Option A (preferred):
- Allocate StrataGrid baseline 28 units reserved. 4 additional units available from shared burst pool (not reserved).
- Implement strict burst preemption policy: HelioWorks gets preemption priority on their reserved lane; StrataGrid burst lane can be preempted with 30-minute notice automated via routing policy.
- Offer StrataGrid a 10% onboarding credit for the first month to offset reduced baseline.
- Impact: HelioWorks unaffected for committed baseline; StrataGrid may see transient throttling during HelioWorks sustained peaks.

Option B (time-shift):
- Move StrataGrid launch window to July 3–21 (full 32 reserved units available then).
- Offer a larger credit + engineering support for migration.
- Impact: delay to StrataGrid launch.

Option C (overcommit with elastic burst from public capacity):
- Short-term cross-region burst to us-west-2 public pool. Slightly higher per-token cost and potentially higher p99 latency.
- Impact: avoids affecting HelioWorks but increases StrataGrid cost and may degrade latency SLAs.

I attached a quick run of gpu_sizing_model.xlsx with estimates and the scheduling overlap heatmap. Ben — can you validate the cost delta for Option C? Lauren — draft two short customer notes (A and B) — one for StrataGrid (external) and one internal-facing escalation summary.

If we can align on Option A we should confirm routing preemption rules, update the runbook (preemption_runbook.md), and get signatures.

Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning
karthik@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Apr 2028 12:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request and conflict notice (SG-4723)

Confirmed numbers from finance and pricing team:
- Option A (partial baseline + preemptible burst) increases operational overhead by ~4% and reduces expected margin by ~6% for the month.
- Option C (cross-region burst) costs ~22% more for token spend and adds ~8–12ms median latency for affected calls.

Recommendation: pursue Option A with the following controls:
1) Hard SLA for baseline 28 units (no preemption).
2) Burst pool up to 48 units with automated preemption window of 30 minutes. Preemption notifications must be sent to customer webhooks and to the ingress router.
3) Provide StrataGrid a 12% onboarding credit and 4 hours of site reliability support during launch week.
4) Contract amendment (small addendum) to SG-4723 documenting preemption rules and credit terms.

Lauren — pls draft the customer addendum and a short email explaining the burst behavior. Kimberly — if you agree, I’ll ops-signoff and we can route DocuSign.

Ben
VP, Revenue Operations
ben@redwood.com
From: Elena Park <elena@stratagrid.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratagrid.com
Date: Sun, 29 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request and conflict notice (SG-4723)

Kimberly — thanks for the quick coordination and to the team for the thoughtful options. Option A is acceptable to StrataGrid provided the preemption details are documented and we get the 12% onboarding credit and the 4-hour SRE support. We accept the 28-unit guaranteed baseline + burst lane to 48 with the 30-minute preemption window.

Please send the addendum and the webhook/notification contract details. Once we have the DocuSign link we’ll get procurement to sign asap.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Park
Head of Platform Ops, StrataGrid
elena@stratagrid.com
